messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream (us-west-2). Error rate rising, multiple clients reporting timeouts. Auto-escalation: paging SRE.
sre_oncall: Ack. I'm on it. Which customers are affected and any seen error codes?
alex: seeing a cluster of stalled connections at the proxy layer (envoy). TLS write stalls + socket buffers fill, then client side timeouts. Logs:
```
envoy [2026-02-20T21:04:12Z] upstream write failed: deadline_exceeded, downstream socket closed after 11.4s
stream-id=0x7f3a client=10.1.2.3:52344
```
maria: ng. Also seeing a backlog on the streaming handler - worker threads blocked on write backpressure. p95/99 both spiking. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/streams/overview?region=us-west-2
jordan: Customer impact: support queue shows 14 tickets in the last 5m complaining about streaming timeouts and partial responses. One enterprise customer (acme-co) hit multiple failed streams, reported in console as 502/timeout. ETA for mitigation please?
sre_oncall: triage plan: 1) enable streaming.fallback (polling fallback) for us-west-2 2) reduce envoy downstream_flush_interval / increase keepalive 3) throttle max_inflight_per_conn on proxies 4) route subset of traffic to dedicated pool. Can eng runtime make the flag changes and routing? incident-bot: runbook link: https://runbook.redwood/streaming/backpressure
maria: recommended short-term envoy tweak (apply to nodes with high stall counts):
```
# envoy config diff (hot-reload)
cluster:
  downstream_keepalive: 30s -> 60s
  downstream_flush_interval: 1s -> 200ms
http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.stream-buffer
    typed_config:
      max_chunk_bytes: 65536 -> 16384
```
eng_runtime: can do the feature toggle and routing. I'll also deploy a temporary weighted route to dedicated nodes. Commands I'm going to run:
```
# enable fallback for region
feature-toggle set streaming.fallback true --scope region:us-west-2 --by=eng_runtime
# route 25% to dedicated pool
rctl route update --service stream --region us-west-2 --weights shared=75 dedicated=25
# restart envoy daemonset on affected nodes (rolling)
kubectl -n prod rollout restart daemonset/envoy-proxy --selector region=us-west-2
```
alex: I'll run a quick check of kernel TCP retransmits and socket_writes on the busiest proxy host. Running:
```
ss -tin state established sport = :443 | grep -c write-blocked
netstat -s | grep retransmitted
```
support_lead: please post templated customer impact blurb after mitigation so I can send to affected accounts. Jordan, compile list of affected orgs.
jordan: list so far: acme-co, boutiqueai, analytics-inc. I'll add full list to the ticket.
eng_runtime: flips feature toggle now.
eng_runtime: feature-toggle set succeeded. streaming.fallback=ON (us-west-2). Pushing weighted route update.
incident-bot: ACTION: feature-toggle/route-update performed by eng_runtime at 2026-02-20T21:06:41Z
sre_oncall: rolling restart of envoy started (minimal disruption, 3 at a time). Watch for second-order latency.
alex: after the fallback + route update, p99 dropped from ~4.2s to ~0.9s within two minutes. Observed fewer write stalls. Adjusting max_inflight_per_conn to 8 on the proxy (down from 32) to reduce head-of-line blocking.
maria: logs show chunk boundary errors reduced after lowering max chunk size. Still seeing occasional clients with long-lived slow readers; we'll need client-side backpressure signals in the long term.
jordan: support notification draft (for review):
```
We experienced intermittent streaming delivery delays in us-west-2 between 21:03-21:12 UTC. Some customers observed partial payloads or timeouts. We have applied a fallback and routing mitigation. If you continue to see errors, please open a ticket and include request IDs.
```
support_lead: LGTM. Send to affected list once we confirm stable for 20m.
eng_runtime: mitigation summary:
- feature streaming.fallback enabled (region-scoped)
- 25% traffic routed to dedicated pool
- envoy keepalive and flush tuned, max_chunk_bytes reduced
- rolling restart of envoy proxies in us-west-2 to pick up config
sre_oncall: monitoring now at p99 ~1s, error rate trending down. Entering 1hr watch. Assigning follow-up: root cause analysis for streaming backpressure (eng_runtime + alex) and customer communication (support_lead + jordan).
incident-bot: PAGED: next oncall (alex) will take postmortem and notify leadership if SLA boundary breached.
alex: taking postmortem. Initial hypotheses: a combination of slow consumer clients causing proxy-level write buffer growth + some recent change in chunk emission logic increased large chunk sizes causing stall amplification. We'll capture flamegraphs and tcpdump on a sample node.
maria: for RCA action items: 1) add prefix/KV caching improvements + protect write loops, 2) expose backpressure metrics per-conn, 3) add ack-based pacing for SSE clients.
sre_oncall: handoff: I've updated the incident doc and added timelines. Next oncall please monitor p99 and error rate for 60m. If p99 goes >2s or error rate >0.5%, re-escalate immediately. Link to incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/7912345678
jordan: customers notified. I'll post follow-up note when watch completes.
support_lead: thanks team. Please include an item in the postmortem to review bulk-client streaming patterns (esp. long-lived slow readers).
alex: closing active mitigation thread — moving to postmortem channel in 30m. Will update the incident ticket with logs and commands run.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied and p99 decreased. Severity: degraded -> watch. Incident handler: alex. Follow-up owners assigned: eng_runtime (RCA), support_lead (customer comms).
